reasons.realCost: Kit's Free plan costs nothing up to 10,000 subscribers, but Creator and Creator Pro's subscriber-tier pricing above their published 1,000-subscriber starting prices of $39 and $79 is shown only inside Kit's own interactive calculator, so the real bill at typical small-business list sizes cannot be predicted from published figures.
reasons.pricingHonesty: Kit publishes the $39 Creator and $79 Creator Pro starting prices and one further breakpoint, but its Help Center does not publish a tier-price table beyond 1,000 subscribers, leaving buyers dependent on the live pricing-page calculator to learn the cost at larger list sizes.
reasons.smallTeamFit: Kit is built around a single creator's own account with a 14-day no-card trial and a Free plan usable without setup help, and frames its Creator plan explicitly as sized for one or two people.
reasons.doesTheJob: Kit combines newsletters, automations, landing pages and digital-product sales in one account, though it is scoped to a single creator's list rather than the multi-client or ecommerce-CRM depth of some competitors.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Kit offers a 30-day money-back guarantee on every paid plan and month-to-month billing with no long contract, though downgrading to a lower subscriber tier when a list shrinks is a manual step rather than automatic.
reasons.trackRecord: Kit raised its Creator and Creator Pro starting prices in October 2025 and applied the new prices to existing customers as well as new ones.

basis: Kit suits a solo creator thanks to its free 10,000-subscriber tier and fast self-serve setup, but its October 2025 price rise reached existing customers and its prices above 1,000 subscribers are shown only in a calculator, which undercuts the predictability a small business needs.
method: Two independent blind passes scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the lower of the two overall scores, because this tool runs an affiliate program we have joined or may join. Pass scores: 3 and 3.
